TF211017.headline: One carton is the minimum
overview: The TF211017 is an AK47-pattern water rifle in two transparent finishes, one smoke grey and one deep red, both showing the internals through the receiver. The distinguishing detail is the LED strip along the flank, which cycles through several colours rather than lighting a single flame at the muzzle the way the rest of the range does. A red-dot style optic sits on the top rail, the muzzle carries a suppressor-style tip, and the reservoir is a drum under the body. The gun is packed two to a display box, which is how a retailer would put it out rather than as a single unit.

That display-box packing produces the most unusual order structure in the catalogue. A carton holds 60 pieces, 30 display boxes, at 0.249 CBM and 23 kg gross, and the 60-piece minimum is exactly one carton. No other model here can be ordered as a single carton, so this is the lowest-commitment entry into the whole range: one carton, 0.249 CBM, 60 pieces. A 20GP takes 112 cartons, 6,720 pieces, which is a lower piece count than most models in this range because the display box adds cube and the drum adds weight.

At $6.51 it sits between the TF210960 submachine gun at $6.13 and the TF199679 two-in-one combo at $7.13. Its case is the display box and the single-carton minimum: a distributor or a small retailer can take one carton of thirty display boxes, put them on a counter, and find out whether the AK47 form sells in their market before committing to anything larger. For a first water gun order in an unproven market, that is a materially different risk profile from the five- and eight-carton minimums elsewhere in the range.
visible_features: AK47-pattern rifle with a drum reservoir under the body
Two transparent finishes: smoke grey and deep red
Multi-colour LED strip along the receiver flank
Red-dot style optic on the top rail and a suppressor-style muzzle
Packed two pieces to a display box, 30 display boxes per carton
60 pieces per carton at 0.249 CBM, a single carton at the 60-piece minimum

TF211526.headline: 350 ml, and the cell is printed on the pack
overview: The TF211526 is a hand-held Gatling gun: a rotating barrel cluster at the front, a carry handle over the top and a pistol grip at the rear, moulded in transparent blue with the barrels left clear so the water shows through. WATERGUN ELECTRIC is printed on the flank. The photograph of the pack contents is unusually specific, and it is the most useful thing about this page: it shows a USB charging lead, a spare USB connector, a small screwdriver and a cylindrical cell labelled Li-ion 18650 3.7V 1200mAh, so the power side of the specification is visible rather than something the buyer has to take on trust.

The 350 ml reservoir in the model name is the number that sells it: 350 ml at continuous fire is a longer run than a drum-fed pistol holds, which is the reason to move up to this form. A carton holds 30 pieces at 0.175 CBM and 20 kg gross, 0.67 kg per unit, and a 20GP takes 160 cartons, 4,800 pieces. The 150-piece minimum is five cartons at 0.875 CBM. The weight per unit is high for the range because of the barrel cluster and the cell, so air freight is the case to check first.

At $9.29 it is the second step in the premium pair, below the TF211527 at $14.50 and above the TF210965 rifle at $10.15. Of the three, this is the one with the capacity argument and the visible cell specification, so it suits a market where the buyer inspects the accessories before ordering. The screwdriver in the box is a small detail with a practical consequence: the cell is meant to be replaced, not thrown away with the unit.

TF212336.headline: Ten pieces to a carton
overview: The TF212336 is a bullpup-style electric water gun: the magazine and firing mechanism sit behind the trigger group rather than in front of it, which keeps the body short while the barrel stays long. Two transparent finishes are produced, blue and smoke, and the body carries a red-dot style optic on the rail and a pump-action foregrip under the barrel. A separate drum magazine is also shown with the unit, alongside the box magazine. The retail box is printed ELECTRIC WATER GUN and ELECTRIC CONTINUOUS FIRING WATER GUN, which describes the automatic action rather than a single shot.

The carton is the least dense in the whole catalogue. Only 10 pieces go into a carton, at 0.096 CBM and 9.2 kg gross, which is 0.92 kg per unit, and a 20GP takes 291 cartons, 2,910 pieces. The 100-piece minimum is ten cartons, 0.96 CBM. Ten cartons to reach the minimum is the highest carton count per entry order here outside the TF210960, and it is the number to look at before quoting: the cube is small per carton, so the freight is manageable, but a buyer cannot enter with one or two cartons the way they can on the AK47.

At $8.16 it sits between the two-in-one models around $7 and the Gatling at $9.29. Its case is the bullpup form and the belt-fed drum, which is the closest this catalogue gets to the look of a squad automatic weapon at a toy price. That is a specific shelf: it appeals to the buyer who wants something more elaborate than an SMG but will not pay the $9 to $14 that the Gatling and the rifle command.

TF199679.headline: Water out of the front, bubbles out of the back
overview: The TF199679 is the two-in-one model: a single blaster that fires water from the muzzle and bubbles from a perforated panel on the rear body, so a child can switch between a water fight and a bubble stream without changing toys. The form is a chunky blaster with a transparent water bottle slung under the front, a top rail with a sight, and a moulded rear stock carrying the bubble vents. It ships two colourways, blue with grey and white, and orange with grey and white, in a printed display box headed WATER AND BUBBLE GUN SERIES and marked 2 IN 1.

This is the bulkiest carton in the water range. A carton holds 36 pieces at 0.30 CBM, the largest cube per carton in this catalogue, at 26.5 kg gross and 0.74 kg per unit. A 20GP takes 93 cartons, 3,348 pieces, and the 180-piece minimum is five cartons, 1.5 CBM. The display box is the reason for the cube: the retail pack is designed to stand on a counter and show the product, which costs space that a plain colour box would not.

At $7.13 it is the cheaper of the two dual-function models, under the TF211492 at $7.27 and well under the TF214001 at $5.49 for a different arrangement. The distinction that matters is how the two functions are laid out. Here the two outlets sit at opposite ends of the body, whereas the TF211492 groups both at the front; how the two are sequenced on the trigger is confirmed per order. For a first dual-function order the display box and the lower price make this the safer test; the simultaneous-fire arrangement is the upgrade.

TF211492.headline: Both functions running from the front
overview: The TF211492 is the model that fires water and bubbles at the same time from the front of the unit rather than from opposite ends. The muzzle throws the water jet through a lit flame effect, and a cylindrical orange module slung under the barrel releases a cluster of bubbles from a perforated front disc, so the child gets both streams from one trigger pull. MACHINE BUBBLE GUN is printed on the flank and the body is a dark grey with orange accents, which is a more muted finish than the transparent blue used across most of the water range.

The pack contents are the fullest in this catalogue. Alongside the gun the photographs show a spare drum, a bottle of bubble solution, two cells, two USB leads and a screwdriver, so the unit arrives able to run and able to be serviced. A carton holds 16 pieces at 0.091 CBM and 10.5 kg gross, 0.66 kg per unit, and a 20GP takes 307 cartons, 4,912 pieces. The 80-piece minimum is five cartons at 0.455 CBM, which is one of the smaller entry orders in the range.

At $7.27 it is the most expensive of the three dual-function models, above the TF199679 at $7.13 and the TF214001 at $5.49, and the gap is thin enough that the decision is about function rather than price. Simultaneous water and bubbles is a genuinely different play pattern from either alternative, and the supplied solution and spare drum mean the first run does not need anything bought separately. For a buyer whose market responds to demonstration, this is the model that sells itself across a counter.

TF214001.headline: The chunky one, with a bottle in the box
overview: The TF214001 is built for a younger hand. The body is short and deep, moulded in black with red, yellow and teal accents, and the moulded grip is a full hand-filling shape rather than a slim pistol grip. Water leaves the muzzle through a lit flame effect and bubbles come out of the round clear outlet at the front of the body, and a multi-colour LED strip runs along the top rear. POWER is printed in large letters along the flank. The box lists it as an electric bubble water gun in 2-in-1 form for ages three and up.

It is also the only water gun here that ships with bubble solution in the box: the photographs show a square screw-top bottle of solution, one cylindrical cell and a USB charging lead, so the product is complete on opening rather than needing a separate purchase. A carton holds 48 pieces at 0.239 CBM and 30 kg gross, 0.63 kg per unit, and a 20GP takes 117 cartons, 5,616 pieces. The 240-piece minimum is five cartons at 1.195 CBM, the largest minimum quantity among the dual-function models.

At $5.49 it is the cheapest dual-function model, below the TF199679 at $7.13 and the TF211492 at $7.27, and that is its whole commercial case: a two-in-one product at a price close to the single-function water guns. The larger 240-piece minimum is the trade-off for the lower unit price. For a buyer whose market is younger children and whose shelf is price-sensitive, this is the model that puts both functions in front of the customer for the least money.
